Script commands run without an implicit shell. On Windows, naming a `.cmd` or `.bat` file as
the command fails with `SCRIPT_START_FAILED`: the process runner proved that it did not start.
This is distinct from `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN`, which needs explicit recovery consent because
an earlier attempt may have produced effects. A proven start refusal permits ordinary Resume,
but Resume and Replay both use the failed run's pinned command, arguments and working-directory
configuration.

quote paths and arguments for `cmd.exe`, rather than inserting untrusted text. For example,
with a working directory containing `build.cmd`, the arguments are `["/d", "/c", "build.cmd"]`.
Publish the corrected definition and start a fresh run. Neither Resume nor Replay applies a
definition change; both retain the old batch-file command. If only an external prerequisite changed, such as
restoring a missing executable, Resume can use the existing pinned definition.

## A provider conversation is missing

`HARNESS_SESSION_MISSING` means the provider no longer has the selected conversation,
for example after removal, expiry or changing the provider's home directory. The
failure names the harness, handle and origin. Plain Resume cannot restore it.

In the run inspector choose **Start fresh session for <node>** only when you want
to repeat that node's authored task without its prior provider conversation. Selected
loop inputs and the configured context mode, model and effort stay the same. Earlier
provider actions are not undone. Leaving the choice untouched keeps the run failed;
reload and gateway restart preserve it. The recovery note records who chose and when.

API callers read the failed event's sequence and post `{ "nodeId": "worker",
"failureSeq": 17 }` to `/runs/{id}/recover-session` with `runs:write`. A stale or
repeated choice returns 409: inspect the current failure before acting again.
Failures recorded by an older gateway without the new typed provenance require a
deliberate new run/replay; upgrading does not rewrite historical failures.

A containing subloop run retains the original non-resumable failure in history.
Recover the failed inference child via its child-run link, then use the API Resume
on the containing run. The gateway verifies the same owned child's later durable
resume and current absence of a runtime failure; before that recovery it rejects Resume.

## Recovery eligibility and Replay (#256)

Read the inspector's explanation for the current action. Resume retains the run ID and follows its next attempt. A completed `SCRIPT_EXIT_CODE` failure remains resumable: fix the program, then Resume. Non-resumable stop/deadline/unconfirmed-termination failures stay unavailable for Resume. A failed child directs recovery to its exact parent, which retries the same child.

Replay is a deliberate new run at a reached node, including inference and subloop nodes, across source run statuses. It runs scripts, provider turns, child runs and deliveries on the new path again; the picker names knowable nodes on possible paths. It never undoes source effects or re-sends source-owned delivery records; the fork performs its own deliveries. A missing session does not prohibit Replay, although a named policy may look up the same missing session again. Use Start fresh session for #265's explicit same-run recovery. A path into the current uncertain script also needs explicit consent that its effect may already have happened.

If `RECOVERY_STALE` names an existing replay ID, open that run. The admitted fork and its observed intent are one transaction; there is no separate consumed-intent-without-fork window. Otherwise refresh and review current eligibility. API/MCP commands send `observedSeq` from that read, and `retryUncertainScript: true` only after deliberate uncertain-script consent. See [ADR-0061](../decisions/ADR-0061-recovery-eligibility.md).

## Layout

- `packages/contracts` - Zod schemas and types. Depends on zod only.
- `packages/domain` - pure logic over the contracts. No I/O.
- `packages/engine` - executor, run manager, node handlers, written against ports. `@graphgoblin/engine/testing` has fakes for every port.
- `packages/infrastructure` - Node implementations of the engine ports, one folder per concern (`src/sqlite`, `src/fs`, `src/process`, `src/http`, `src/scheduler`), each with its own `index.ts` and an `@graphgoblin/infrastructure/<folder>` subpath. Folders may import each other.

- `apps/*` - composition roots: `api`, `mcp`, `web`, `plugin-codex`, `plugin-claude`.
- `tooling/` - shared config and the repository gate scripts.

Layer rules are enforced by `pnpm check:layers` (declared workspace dependencies) and `pnpm check:deps` (dependency-cruiser). Reach other packages only through their `@graphgoblin/*` entry points.

Node 22 LTS is the supported runtime; installation, development and gates need Node 22.22.2 or later, and other majors are unsupported. Select it for the whole shell before running commands. On this Windows host that is the project-scoped runtime, leaving the machine's own Node untouched: `$env:PATH = "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\codex-runs\GraphGoblin\runtime\node-v22.23.4-win-x64;$env:PATH"` in PowerShell, or `export PATH="$HOME/.claude/codex-runs/GraphGoblin/runtime/node-v22.23.4-win-x64:$PATH"` in Git Bash. Confirm `node --version` reports `v22.22.2` or later. `.nvmrc`, CI and the container use major 22 (CI and the container take the latest 22.x); root `engines.node` and `devEngines.runtime` declare `^22.22.2`, with `onFail: error` refusing every pnpm command on an older Node 22 or another major. pnpm runs package scripts with the first `node` on PATH. Run gates through pnpm: calling `node_modules/.bin/turbo` directly bypasses this check, and Turbo's cache key ignores the running Node version. See ADR-0040 and ADR-0058.

## Rules

- `tooling` participates in the shared Vitest V8 coverage gate and the Turbo lint pipeline; its independent built-app acceptance suites remain separate.
- Every package must keep unit-test coverage at or above 90% of lines and branches. `pnpm test:coverage` fails otherwise. Do not lower thresholds or add exclusions beyond generated code.

Node at runtime loads `dist/`, so run `pnpm build` before starting an app. A new TypeScript workspace package must follow the same export-map shape. `tooling` tests drive the built API and web app: Turbo builds them first, and a direct package test needs `pnpm build` first.

- Relative imports use explicit `.js` extensions (NodeNext). Zod 4: use `.prefault({})` for object defaults whose fields have defaults.
- Keep docs in sync: a behaviour change updates the relevant numbered doc; a decision change adds an ADR.
- Clean design over backward compatibility, until the owner says otherwise (2026-10-04): the product is not released and has no production users. A schema change within the current format is an ordinary Drizzle migration that keeps existing data; Drizzle migrations are for schema changes only. ```
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm test:coverage
pnpm lint
pnpm docs:generate  # regenerate docs/reference after a node schema or route change
pnpm check          # typecheck, lint, layers, deps, coverage, licences, generated docs
